title: PWA (Progressive Web App)
seoTitle: What Is a PWA? Progressive Web Apps Explained
seoDescription: A PWA is a website that installs and behaves like an app. When a PWA can replace a native app, offline use, costs and limits on iPhone and Android.
summary: A PWA (Progressive Web App) is a website built so it can be installed on a phone's home screen, open full-screen, work offline in part, and send notifications, without going through an app store. For many business tools it offers most of an app's benefits at a lower cost.

dataPoints.label: Installs from
dataPoints.value: The browser, no app store needed

dataPoints.label: Works offline
dataPoints.value: Yes, for cached screens and queued data entry, when designed for it

dataPoints.label: Cost versus native apps
dataPoints.value: Usually lower: one codebase for web, Android and iPhone

dataPoints.label: Limits
dataPoints.value: Some device features and iPhone background behaviour are more restricted than native apps

body:
## When a PWA is a good choice

- Internal tools for staff: field sales, delivery, inspections.
- Customer portals used occasionally.
- Products that need fast updates without store approvals.

## When a native app is better

- Heavy use of device hardware such as Bluetooth or background location.
- Consumer products where app-store presence matters.

See [progressive web apps](/blog/progressive-web-apps-when-a-website-can-replace-an-app) and [mobile app or mobile-friendly web app](/blog/do-you-need-a-mobile-app-or-a-mobile-friendly-web-app).

faqs.q: Can a PWA send push notifications on iPhone?
faqs.a: Yes, on recent iOS versions once the user adds the PWA to the home screen, with some limits compared with native apps.

faqs.q: Can I publish a PWA on Google Play?
faqs.a: Yes, it can be packaged for the Play Store if store presence is needed.
